name: Borde, 'Topology change in classical general relativity' (arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, 30 Jun 1994), Sec. IX bullet 5 with Theorem 1 (Sec. IV): under causal compactness, topology change forces a closed timelike curve even if incomplete geodesics are admitted -- 'singularity escape fails' under the standard incomplete-geodesic definition

source.located: arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1. The quotation is Sec. IX 'Concluding Comments', 5th misconception bullet ('Closed-universe topology change leads either to closed timelike curves or to a singularity'). The theorem behind it is Sec. IV Theorem 1 (with the non-time-orientable variant in Sec. VII). Definitions: Sec. II.A (interpolating spacetime, smooth Lorentz metric, S1/S2 spacelike, compact timelike tube T), Sec. III.B (causal compactness: closure of I(p) compact for every p), Sec. III.E (open universes, 'externally simple'). 'The very end of this paper' that the bullet points to is IX.C (degenerate metrics). Tipler 1977 and Geroch 1967 are NAMED-NOT-READ, known here only as Borde restates them.

published_statement: Sec. IX, bullet 5: 'Closed-universe topology change leads either to closed timelike curves or to a singularity. The truth of this depends on the definition of a singularity. If the standard incomplete-geodesic definition is used, then this statement is not true: as long as the causal compactness condition is met, causality violations have to occur when the topology changes, even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. But, other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true: this is briefly discussed at the very end of this paper.' Sec. IV: 'By "causality violation" it is meant that there is at least one closed timelike curve.' Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' Sec. VII: 'a causally compact spacetime that interpolates between non-empty boundaries S1 and S2 and which does not have closed timelike curves must (a) be diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and (b) hence be time-orientable.' Abstract, on Theorem 3 (the dynamical result, a different theorem): 'it does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities (of the standard incomplete-geodesic variety)'.
published_hypotheses: M is a connected n-manifold (any n; 'No assumption is made about the dimension'), smooth, Hausdorff and paracompact (Sec. II), with boundary S1 u S2 u T, where T is compact and possibly empty. If T is non-empty: T meets each S_i in its boundary, the boundaries of S1 and S2 are diffeomorphic, and T is diffeomorphic to (boundary of S1) x [0,1] (Sec. II.A).

There is a SMOOTH (non-degenerate) Lorentz metric in which S1 and S2 are spacelike and T is timelike (Sec. II.A). Sec. VIII (C^0 metrics) and IX.C (degenerate metrics) name relaxing this as a way out.
Causal compactness: the closure of I(p) is compact for every p in M (Sec. III.B).
Theorem 1: M is time-oriented. Sec. VII extends the result to non-time-orientable metrics when S1 and S2 are both NON-EMPTY. When one boundary is empty, a non-time-orientable metric can avoid CTCs.

For open or asymptotically flat universes, M is the causally compact region of a larger 'externally simple' spacetime: outside that region, the initial and final surfaces are diffeomorphic (Sec. III.E).
Topology change means S1 is not diffeomorphic to S2 (the conclusion of Theorem 1 is negated).
NO geodesic-completeness assumption (Theorem 1's statement has none; C2a).

The conclusion 'the escape fails' holds for the STANDARD incomplete-geodesic definition of singularity. Borde says 'other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true' and points to IX.C (metrics that vanish or degenerate at isolated points).
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED (the definition condition is flattened into a boolean) -- create.py:187 SINGULARITY_ESCAPES = False keeps the condition only in a trailing code comment ('# Borde: not under the standard defn'). The check at create.py:289 prints 'accepting a singularity escapes it ... False' with no definition condition (C6b). Borde makes the claim conditional ('The truth of this depends on the definition of a singularity ... other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true'; C1d, C1e), and the other definition he points to is IX.C, degenerate metrics, which he says 'might well prove to be the correct approach'. Under Borde's own terms the boolean is exact only for incomplete-geodesic singularities.

DROPPED (the causal-compactness condition in the prose summary) -- create.py:341-342: 'I expected "accept a singularity" to be the way out and it is not: causality violations occur even if incomplete geodesics are admitted.' The condition 'as long as the causal compactness condition is met' is gone (C6d). The same file keeps it elsewhere: create.py:69-71, the BORDE_SINGULARITY string at 200-202, and the printed [:66] prefix at 290 (C6c). So this is a lapse in one summary, not in the file's logic. It matters because the singularity most people mean (a point removed, or a hole) BREAKS causal compactness and so falls under IX.A, not under this sentence (C4b: dropping cc leaves no-CTC satisfiable). specthm.py:1655-1665 W-create-ncc keeps that case separate ('a singular throat is M's own mechanism').

CONFLATED (kinematic sentence carrying a dynamical conclusion) -- index3.py:884: 'accepting a singularity does NOT buy topology change. Borde -- as long as the causal compactness condition is met, causality violations have to occur ... EVEN IF INCOMPLETE GEODESICS ARE ADMITTED'. The quoted sentence says a singularity does not AVOID CTCs. It does not say topology change is unobtainable: kinematically, topology change is bought at the price of a CTC (Sec. III; Borde's 2-d examples). 'Does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities' is Theorem 3's conclusion (abstract; C1g), and Theorem 3 adds dimension >= 3, the null generic condition (i) and the null convergence condition (ii). The next clause of index3.py:884 does cite Theorem 3's dynamics separately. So both statements are true under their own hypotheses, but the headline clause rests on the wrong one of the two.

DROPPED (inherited from the sibling audit, re-confirmed here) -- the smooth non-degenerate Lorentz metric. specthm.py:614-615 H_cc carries causal compactness alone, and the GEROCH-BORDE fact at specthm.py:1838-1844 encodes created & cc -> ctc. z3 C4d gives a countermodel without 'smooth'; C4e shows the fact is entailed once smooth and time-orientation (or non-empty boundaries) are added. Removing non-degeneracy is exactly the route (IX.C; later Dowker-Surya, Garcia-Heveling) that gives topology change with no CTC.

UNSTATED SCOPE (a named hypothesis the tree does not write) -- applying Theorem 1 to throat creation in an open, asymptotically flat space requires the change to sit in a causally compact region of an EXTERNALLY SIMPLE spacetime: outside a compact region, S1 and S2 must be diffeomorphic (Sec. III.E; C2d). An intra-universe handle (R^3 -> R^3 # S^1xS^2, which is what create.py:24 'R^3 IS SIMPLY CONNECTED AND A WORMHOLE IS NOT' describes) satisfies this, since S1 and S2 differ only inside a ball. Creating a NEW asymptotic region (an inter-universe throat, S^2 x R, which is simply connected) is not a compactly supported change, and Theorem 1 as stated does not reach it. The tree's 'created' literal (specthm.py:1651-1652) does not say which kind of throat is meant.

SCOPE TRANSFER (licensed, recorded) -- the quoted sentence sits under a CLOSED-universe bullet header (C1c), and the tree applies it to an open case. The sentence's own condition, 'as long as the causal compactness condition is met', together with Theorem 1 and Sec. III.E, licenses the transfer to causally compact open cases. The license is Theorem 1, not the bullet.

WEAKENED IN THE TREE'S DISFAVOUR (an under-claim, harmless) -- specthm.py:1910 PROP_TEXT 'ctc' = 'a closed causal curve'. Borde's conclusion is a closed TIMELIKE curve (C1f), which is stronger. The tree claims less than the source.

KEPT CORRECTLY -- create.py:200-202 is verbatim (C1a); create.py:65-66 'a condition satisfied in a very wide range of situations' is verbatim from the abstract (C1b); the condition 'even if incomplete geodesics are admitted' is backed by Theorem 1, whose statement has no completeness hypothesis (C2a); the CTC is placed 'in the interpolating region, not shown to be at the seat' (specthm.py:1910-1911, 1655-1657), which matches Theorem 1.

rederivation.outcome: 33/33 checks agree, exit 0 (output in rederive/gr-qc_9406053_causal-compactness.out). C0: source md5 matches. C1a-h: both quotations the tree attributes are verbatim, and their context is read: the bullet is the closed-universe misconception, the conclusion is conditioned on 'the standard incomplete-geodesic definition', 'other definitions ... may make the statement true' points to IX.C degenerate metrics, 'causality violation' means at least one CTC, and 'even at the price of singularities' belongs to Theorem 3 in the abstract. C2a-e: Theorem 1's statement has no completeness or geodesic hypothesis; its hypotheses are time-oriented, causally compact, interpolating and no CTC; the smooth-Lorentz-metric requirement and the externally-simple open case are in the text. C3 (sympy): on the Clifton-Pohl torus g = 2dxdy/(x^2+y^2) mod (x,y)~2(x,y), which is compact and so causally compact (Borde III.C), x = 1/(1-t), y = 0 is an affinely parametrised null geodesic that crosses infinitely many fundamental domains before t = 1, so it is incomplete, and c(s) = 2^s(1,-1) is a smooth closed timelike curve with g(c',c') = -(ln 2)^2. Compactness and geodesic incompleteness therefore coexist, and the CTC is present anyway: the 'even if incomplete geodesics are admitted' clause is not vacuous. This is an illustration on a manifold without boundary, not a proof of Theorem 1. C4 (z3), on the propositional skeleton of Theorem 1 with Sec. VII: tc & cc & smooth & to & ~ctc is UNSAT whether 'incomplete' is true or false (incompleteness plays no role); dropping cc makes it SAT (IX.A open); S1 empty with a non-time-orientable metric makes ~ctc SAT (Sec. VII); the tree's created & cc -> ctc is not entailed without smooth and is entailed with it. C5: 8,476 finite flows (N <= 5) checked; every flow line trapped in a finite set closes up, which is the discrete shadow of Theorem 1's accumulation step. C6: tree sites read-only, drift positions confirmed. Not machine-checked: Theorem 1's full proof (limit points of integral curves in a compact closure of I+(b), openness of I-(q)), which is infinite-dimensional; only its finite skeleton and its logical form are checked.

later_literature.ref: arXiv:2202.09833v4 (Garcia-Heveling 2022/2024), 'Topology change with Morse functions: progress on the Borde-Sorkin conjecture'
later_literature.what: Builds out the 'other definitions of a singularity' Borde points to (IX.C). Metrics that degenerate at isolated Morse points give topology change WITHOUT CTCs: 'the only way to have topology change without time travel is by allowing the spacetime metric to degenerate'. So the tree's unconditional SINGULARITY_ESCAPES = False fails for a degenerate-metric singularity, while Borde's conditional sentence stands. It also notes that non-compact slices allow topology change without CTCs or singular points (Sanchez, NAMED-NOT-READ), which is the non-causally-compact side.

later_literature.what: An explicit wormhole nucleation in which the naked singularity of a 0-surgery is removed by Misner's connected sum, so that 'the singularity is replaced by a region containing closed timelike curves'. This is exactly the trade the quoted sentence describes: removing the singularity to get a smooth metric does not avoid the CTC.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: it does not bite, and the evidence is structural. The result is a theorem of Lorentzian differential topology with NO numerical input. Theorem 1 uses no field equation, no energy condition, no measured constant and no completeness assumption (C2a; Borde IX: 'purely kinematical'). No later datum can move its conclusion, so the data_at_publication list is empty by inspection, not by omission. What came later was not data but relaxed HYPOTHESES: degenerate (Morse) metrics (Dowker-Surya 1998; Garcia-Heveling 2022), which give topology change without CTCs. Borde anticipated exactly this ('other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true'; IX.C 'might well prove to be the correct approach'). So the 1994 conclusion is unchanged on its own terms. What the later work changes is the reach of the tree's UNCONDITIONAL boolean, and that is a hypothesis issue (NARROWED), not a data issue.
grade_evidence: Borde's statement STANDS as published. It is quoted verbatim (C1a-b); the theorem behind it, Theorem 1, has no completeness hypothesis (C2a), so 'even if incomplete geodesics are admitted' follows as stated; the logical skeleton checks in z3 (C4a/a': UNSAT with or without incompleteness); a compact, geodesically incomplete Lorentzian manifold with an explicit CTC exists (C3, Clifton-Pohl), so the clause is not vacuous; and no datum enters. The tree's USE is narrower than the tree states it, at four named sites. (1) create.py:187/289 SINGULARITY_ESCAPES = False and its check label are unconditional, but Borde conditions the claim on the standard incomplete-geodesic definition and names degenerate-metric singularities (IX.C) as a possible way out. Later work (Garcia-Heveling 2202.09833) realises that route without CTCs. The comment at create.py:187 keeps the condition; the check output does not. (2) create.py:341-342 drops the causal-compactness condition in its summary; the rest of the file keeps it. (3) index3.py:884 attaches Theorem 3's dynamical conclusion ('does NOT buy topology change', which needs dim >= 3 and curvature conditions (i),(ii)) to a kinematic quotation that only says CTCs are not avoided. (4) H_cc/GEROCH-BORDE (specthm.py:614-615, 1838-1844) drops the smooth non-degenerate metric hypothesis (C4d countermodel). The externally-simple scope for an open-space throat is also unstated. Not WRONG: nothing Borde states is refuted, and the tree's operative encoding (created & cc -> ctc, the CTC in the interpolating region) holds once smooth, non-degenerate, time-oriented-or-non-empty-boundaries and externally-simple are added. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: there is no datum. Not plain STANDS: conditions the source states are dropped at named sites, which is NARROWED's definition.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restores the conditions it drops -- SINGULARITY_ESCAPES qualified in its check output as 'under the standard incomplete-geodesic definition and causal compactness', create.py:341-342 restating causal compactness, index3.py:884's headline tied to Theorem 3's hypotheses (or reworded to 'does not avoid a CTC'), and H_cc carrying the smooth non-degenerate metric and externally-simple scope. To WRONG: a smooth, non-degenerate, time-oriented, causally compact interpolating spacetime with S1 not diffeomorphic to S2 and no CTC, which would refute Theorem 1. None is known, and C4/C5 find none in the finite skeleton. To OPEN: loss of the source text. The md5-checked full text is held in scratchpad/d67/src.
